newsitem.title: USA: Mass. House takes up $4.1 bln in bond issues.
newsitem.headline: Mass. House takes up $4.1 bln in bond issues.

text.p: The Massachusetts House of Representatives is expected to debate $4.1 billion in bond issues Wednesday, including funding for the $10.7 billion Central Artery/Third Harbor Crossing project.

The House Ways and Means Committee voted out the $3.7 billion transportation bond bill that funds road and bridge projects statewide and makes Massachusetts eligible for the federal money needed to build the Central Artery project.

The committee made some amendments to the big transportation bond bill. The measure authorizes Gov. William Weld's administration to borrow $1.2 billion for the Big Dig in anticipation of future federal transportation grants -- something of a gamble.

But an amendment adopted by Ways and Means limits the amount of those Grant Anticipation Notes to $450 million until Washington decides later this year how much will be allotted under the next round of transportation aid to the states.

The transportation bond totals $3.869 billion and covers two year's worth of transportation spending. It authorizes more than $2 billion for the Central Artery project; $750 million from the state's accounts for roads and bridges; and $504 million more in road and bridge work statewide that is reimbursable by the federal government.
The Ways and Means committee also voted out a bill providing $200 million for the redevelopment of Fort Devens.
The Fort Devens bill would provide the cash necessary to turn the closed Army base into a multipurpose transportation and industrial center.
